header.running_head: Rasulullaah ﷺ is Particular about Dispatching the Army of Hadhrat Usaama bin Zaid (RA) even on his Deathbed, after which Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) also Gives the Same Importance to the Matter When he Becomes the Khalifah

blocks.text: Usaama (RA) and not to remove it from the staff until Hadhrat Usaama (RA) had led the Muslims in battle. Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) says, "I then took the flag to the house of Hadhrat Usaama (RA), after which I took it flying to Shaam with Hadhrat Usaama (RA). I then returned it to the house of Hadhrat Usaama (RA) where it stood flying until he passed away."
Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Insists on Dispatching the Army of Hadhrat Usaama (RA) in Compliance with the Orders of Rasulullaah ﷺ

When the news of Rasulullaah ﷺ's demise reached the other Arabs, many of them renounced Islaam. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said to Usaama (RA), "Proceed whence Rasulullaah ﷺ had commanded you to go." Consequently, the army started to march and camped where they were previously camped. Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) also took the flag to the previous camp. This (decision to dispatch the army) did not appeal to the senior Sahabah (RA). Consequently, Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA), Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) and Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid (RA) approached Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). They said, "O successor of Rasulullaah ﷺ! Everywhere the Arabs are rebelling against you and you will not be able to do anything by separating this large army from yourself. Rather use them to combat the Murtaddeen (those who have forsaken Islaam). Another concern we have is that we fear that Madinah may be attacked while there are only women and children here. Why do you not postpone the dispatching of this army against the Romans until stability returns and the Murtaddeen have either returned to the Deen they have left or are destroyed by the sword. You are then at liberty to dispatch Usaama (RA). We are confident that the Romans will not be marching against us yet."
After listening to everything they had to say, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) asked, "Does anyone have anything else to add?" They replied, "No. you have heard everything we have to say." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, "I swear by the Being Who controls my life! I shall dispatch this army even if I knew that wild animals would eat me in Madinah (without them here to defend me). This has to be the first task I shall undertake (as Khalifah). How can I not do it when revelation had been descending on Rasulullaah ﷺ from the heavens as he kept saying, 'Dispatch the army of Usaama.' Of course, there is one thing that I need to speak to Usaama about. It is that Umar stays behind with us (in Madinah) because we cannot do without him. By Allaah! I have no idea whether Usaama will do so or not. I swear by Allaah that if he refuses I shall not compel him to concede." The Sahabah (RA) then realised that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was determined to send the army of Hadhrat Usaama (RA).
